findings.text: Builds a self-checking program that exercises one shift operation across widths and source modes. The builder selects a bit width from flags, reserves a fixed budget, and for each of four seed operands iterates every valid shift amount, emitting operand setup, the operation under test, a host-computed expected value, and early termination on mismatch. On success it publishes the buffer and length into the test object.

Twelve thin wrappers fix operation, source mode and width for the common shift builder, covering logical left, logical right and arithmetic right shifts in 64-bit and 32-bit forms, each with immediate and register shift amounts.

Builds a self-checking program for aliased shift where the value shifted also supplies the amount. The builder walks every amount below the active width, applies the operation with a single register in both roles, compares against a host reference truncated in 32-bit mode, and fails fast on mismatch, otherwise reporting success.
Six wrappers bind the aliased shift builder to each shift operation in 64-bit and 32-bit widths.

The small helper derives an operand by scaling a power of two selected by a magnitude index with a sign choice and then adding a small delta, yielding clustered values around powers of two including negative cases.

Generates a large self-checking program by enumerating two operand patterns through a caller emitter. It sizes the buffer with a dry-run query, allocates it, emits a failure-default prologue, then enumerates cross-product magnitudes with sign combinations and small neighborhoods followed by a same-magnitude larger-neighborhood sweep, and appends a success marker and termination.
The small neighborhood extent used by the first pattern sweep equals one, so each magnitude contributes a single central value per sign combination in that phase.
The larger neighborhood extent used by the second same-magnitude sweep equals five, widening coverage around each power of two.
The configured repetition count for pattern suites equals one.

Four emitters share a two-phase contract: with no output buffer they report a fixed worst-case cost of seven for immediate forms and nine for register forms, and otherwise they optionally emit operand setup, execution and expected-value comparison only when the host reference deems the pair valid, applying signed encoding selection and low-half truncation as appropriate.

Four dispatch helpers bind operand bit widths and emitter choice: immediate forms pair a wide destination space with a narrow source space while register forms use wide spaces for both, forwarding operation and option flags from callers.
Nine constructors cover move, bitwise, arithmetic and unsigned divide and remainder with immediate sources in 64-bit mode through the shared 64-bit immediate dispatcher with default options.
Four constructors select signed divide and remainder with immediate sources in 64-bit and 32-bit modes through the corresponding immediate dispatchers with the signed option enabled.
Nine constructors cover move, bitwise, arithmetic and unsigned divide and remainder with immediate sources in 32-bit mode through the shared 32-bit immediate dispatcher with default options.
Nine constructors cover move, bitwise, arithmetic and unsigned divide and remainder with register sources in 64-bit mode through the shared 64-bit register dispatcher.
Nine constructors cover move, bitwise, arithmetic and unsigned divide and remainder with register sources in 32-bit mode through the shared 32-bit register dispatcher.

Builds a program replaying one immediate operation across every general register, using fixed destination and immediate operands with shift amounts constrained to low bits, a signed variant selecting negative destinations and signed encoding, and per-register verification of low and high result halves with failure reporting tied to the host source line.

Twelve constructors exercise move, bitwise, shift, arithmetic and unsigned divide and remainder with immediate sources across all registers in 64-bit mode through the shared register-sweep builder with default options.
Two constructors exercise signed divide and remainder with immediate sources across all registers in 64-bit mode through the shared register-sweep builder with the signed option.

Twelve constructors exercise move, bitwise, shift, arithmetic and unsigned divide and remainder with immediate sources across all registers in 32-bit mode through the shared register-sweep builder with the 32-bit option.
Two constructors exercise signed divide and remainder with immediate sources across all registers in 32-bit mode through the shared register-sweep builder with combined width and signed options.

Builders fail cleanly with an out-of-memory status when allocation fails without publishing a buffer, and they assert exact or bounded instruction counts after generation, so size miscalculations trap during construction rather than executing a truncated program.
